baseline.limits: Six scalar types plus NULL; signed values vary by row, binary covers all 256 byte values. Includes scalar validation, formatting, framed-row construction and allocator work. Reuses each backend buffer; output escapes optimization. Excludes metadata, TLS, sockets, authority and storage. Framed bytes are database-protocol application bytes, not network traffic. Local observations, not a throughput or latency guarantee.

Actual TSR1/TCP1 encode/decode with independent scalar checks; one-row control versus full batches, initial schema/observation and verified terminal count. Counts backing allocation, resize and remap attempts and successes, frees and bytes. Encoder peak includes columns, scratch and frame; decoder peak excludes the borrowed input frame and stack/schema buffers. Each batch releases all accounted allocations. Timings exclude fixture generation and independent verification; include codec validation and initial metadata. No socket, service, query or storage work; no network throughput guarantee.

Actual TSR1/TCP1 encode/decode with independent scalar checks; one-row control versus full batches, initial schema/observation and verified terminal count. Backing alloc/growing-resize/remap attempts are forbidden after fixed admission; internal bounded reservations are reported separately. Encoder reserves 4 MiB columns/scratch plus 4 MiB frame; decoder reserves 8 MiB excluding borrowed frame and stack/schema buffers. Reset frees live contents while the entire reserve remains charged. Timings exclude fixture generation and independent verification; include codec validation and initial metadata. No socket, service, query, storage or OS-allocation claim; no network throughput guarantee.
